beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:epic, measured]In {146|one forty-six} BCE, Rome destroyed its great rival, ^Carthage. [act:epic, darker]Then, the story goes, it ^salted the earth, so nothing would ever grow ^again. [act:a wry turn, lighter]At least, that's the ^story.
[d:tension][act:leaning in, intrigued][tune:fall]The real one is ^stranger, and it starts with a secret ^harbour.

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]Carthage stood on the coast of North Africa, beside today's ^Tunis. [act:setting the stakes]A trading power, rich from the ^sea, that fought Rome for more than a ^century.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:precise, a telling detail]After losing a great battle at ^Zama, in {202|two oh two} BCE, it was allowed just ^ten warships. [p:0.93][act:a simple picture, wry]A navy you could count on your ^fingers.

[d:build][act:impressed, building]Yet archaeologists found a round war ^harbour. [p:0.93][act:vivid]About three hundred and twenty-five metres across: three football pitches, end to ^end. [p:0.9][act:counting, impressed]All around its rim, and on an island in the middle, sheds for about a hundred and ^seventy ships. [act:explaining]A ship shed is a long roofed ramp: a garage for one ^warship.
[d:aside][act:dry, amused]For a fleet of ^ten. [act:wry, a raised eyebrow][tune:fall]That's a lot@amount of empty ^garages.

[d:build][act:grave, sober]Then, in {146|one forty-six} BCE, after a long ^siege, Rome took the ^city. [act:heavy, quiet]It was ^burned, and its people killed or ^enslaved. [act:quiet, plain]That much, the ancient writers ^describe. [act:even][tune:fall]Fire and ruin, ^yes.

[d:reveal][act:the twist, precise][tune:rise]And the ^salt? [act:plain, clear]Scholars checked every surviving ancient account of the ^war. [act:plain, clear][tune:fall]No ancient writer ^mentions it. [p:0.93][act:revealing, a small smile]The story first appears in a modern history book, from {1930|nineteen thirty}. [act:a simple picture]A rumour born more than two thousand years after the ^event.

[d:build][go:5|0][act:the irony, warm]And the ground was fine. [act:the irony, warm]Within about a century, Rome ^rebuilt Carthage, as one of its greatest ^cities. [act:a dry smile][tune:fall]Hardly the fate of a poisoned ^field.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]Salted ^earth? [act:the verdict, firm][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:the other half, confident]A hidden war harbour, for a navy it wasn't ^allowed? [act:sure][tune:fall]That part is ^real.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, a small smile]Some myths are ancient. [act:quiet, pointed][tune:fall]This one is barely a ^century old.
